Take-home Exercise 3: Geospatial Analytics for Urban Sustainability

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source

Where Singapore’s HDB residents board the train in the morning, and how the Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line would change that

A Huff model, calibrated on LTA tap-in counts and the dwelling units of every HDB block, that estimates morning boardings at each MRT and LRT station and predicts how the planned JRL and CRL stations would share them.

Author
Affiliation

Jedidiah Asaf Tallulembang

ISSS626 Geospatial Analytics and Applications

Published

November 14, 2026

Abstract

This report builds a model of where people living in HDB flats board the train on a weekday morning, and uses it to ask what the planned Jurong Region Line (JRL) and Cross Island Line (CRL) would change.

The model is a Huff model. It shares the 1.18 million dwelling units of 10,817 HDB blocks among the stations around each block, giving more to stations that are closer and to stations that are more attractive. It is calibrated against three months of LTA tap-in counts (August to October 2026) at the 148 stations that have HDB homes around them.

Tested on stations it was not fitted to, the model ranks stations well (rank correlation 0.90) but its estimate for any single station is typically about a third off. Stations that serve more lines, and stations with more shops and services around them, are associated with more boardings; stations served only by LRT with far fewer.

In the network the brief asks about (today’s plus the JRL and CRL phase 1), the new stations with the most HDB homes around them, Tengah Plantation, Serangoon North and Pasir Ris East, have the largest modelled morning boardings. Several JRL and CRL stations in industrial, university and airport areas have almost none; this says that few HDB residents live near them, not that nobody will use them. Because the model holds the number of homes fixed, the new lines redistribute boardings rather than add them: Chinese Garden, Lakeside and Pioneer lose the most.

As a value-added analysis, I let the effect of distance differ by region. Residents of the North-East and West appear about twice as sensitive to distance as those in the Central region; the regional model predicts held-out stations better, and the main conclusions hold under it.

Executive summary · Repository

1 Why this matters

Singapore plans its rail network years ahead of the people who will ride it. LTA builds some stations as shells and opens them when the riders arrive, and sometimes they arrive late. Hume station on the Downtown Line was finished in 2015 and opened on 28 February 2025. Buangkok and Woodleigh stayed closed when the North East Line opened in 2003, because too few people were expected to use them. Deciding when a station opens, and how a new line will change the stations around it, needs an estimate of demand before anyone has used the station.

This exercise builds that estimate for the two lines under construction: the Jurong Region Line in the west, and phase 1 of the Cross Island Line from Aviation Park to Bright Hill.

A station’s catchment is not a hard boundary. A block of flats between two stations belongs to neither: some of its residents walk to one and some to the other, depending on how far each is and what each offers. A Huff model describes exactly that, which is why it is the method used here.

2 Research question and objectives

Where do HDB residents board the train in the weekday morning peak, and how would the planned JRL and CRL stations change that?

The brief sets three objectives. Table 1 shows where each of its tasks is answered.

  1. Calibrate a probabilistic spatial interaction (Huff) model that estimates morning boardings at each station from where people live, how far each station is, and what each station offers.
  2. Use it to predict morning boardings at the planned JRL and CRL stations.
  3. Show how the new stations would change the boardings and catchments of the stations already open.

3 Data and study design

3.1 What exactly is being modelled

The brief asks for station-level ridership. This report models one well-defined part of it, and it is worth being precise about what that part is.

  • Boardings are tap-ins: people entering a station through the fare gates.
  • The time window is weekday mornings, 06:00 to 09:00, averaged over August, September and October 2026. Values are boardings per month in that window.
  • Riders come from home. In the morning most trips start at home, so the people boarding at a station mostly live near it. That is the assumption a residential catchment model needs. Later in the day it fails: a central-area station boards thousands of people in the evening who live nowhere near it (Figure 1).
  • Homes are HDB flats. The number of HDB dwelling units in each block is the “local market potential”. HDB flats house about four in five Singapore residents, and they are the only homes with a public, block-level count. Private housing is not included, which matters (section 4.3).
  • A station is one place. An interchange such as Jurong East counts once, whatever the number of lines it serves.

Table 2 separates what is measured from what is assumed, because the conclusions depend on the difference.

3.2 Data sources

The brief recommends the origin-destination version of the passenger data. On the day I ran the analysis, DataMall refused that endpoint for my account with a quota error, while the station-level endpoint worked. For a model of where people board, the station-level counts are all that is needed: where each trip ends plays no part in it. LTA’s bus stop file also could not be downloaded by script, so OpenStreetMap supplies the bus stops (5,668 of them).

code 
d <- ex |> st_drop_geometry() |> mutate(in_fit = du_1km >= CAL_MIN_DU_1KM)
lab <- d |> filter(name %in% c("Yishun", "Woodlands", "Tampines", "Raffles Place", "Tanjong Pagar",
                               "Newton", "Kranji", "Changi Airport", "Tuas Link", "Punggol", "Jurong East", "Downtown"))
ggplot(d, aes(tapout_am, tap_am)) +
  geom_abline(colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = in_fit), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = name), size = 2.8, colour = PAL$ink, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL$accent, `FALSE` = PAL$loss_lt),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "HDB homes nearby: fitted", `FALSE` = "Few or no HDB homes within 1 km"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Tap-outs, weekdays 06:00 to 09:00, per month (log scale)", y = "Tap-ins, per month (log scale)",
       caption = "Source: LTA DataMall, Passenger Volume by Train Stations, mean of Aug, Sep and Oct 2026.") +
  theme_ex03(grid = "both")

4 Data preparation and quality checks

Every check quoted in this section is computed in R/04b_diagnostics.R.

4.1 Placing every HDB block

The number of homes and the building outlines come in two files with no shared key. The property file names a block by number and a shortened street name (“1 BEDOK STH AVE 1”); the building file by number, a street code (“BEA09N”) and a postal code. Matching on block number alone is wrong, because the same block number appears in many towns.

The street code turned out to be one code per street (657 street names, 660 codes). So I looked up one block per street in OneMap, Singapore’s official address search, and matched the postal code it returned to a building outline. That gives a complete street-to-code lookup (R/01_street_codes.R), and with it 10,734 of the 10,817 residential blocks join to their outline. The remaining 83, mostly new Tengah blocks that are not yet in the building file, were looked up one by one and kept as points.

The checks: no block was matched to two outlines (0 duplicates), no two blocks share a location (0), no geometry is empty (0), and the total of 1,179,156 dwelling units equals the total in the property file. All distances are measured in metres in SVY21 (EPSG:3414). Each block is represented by a point inside its outline (st_point_on_surface()), which, unlike a centroid, cannot fall outside an L-shaped block.

code 
s_all <- lines_sf(stations)
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = origins, aes(size = du), colour = PAL$muted, alpha = 0.25, stroke = 0) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind == "Existing"), shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = PAL$ink, size = 1.1, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind != "Existing"), aes(fill = kind), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 2.3, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 1.6, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(caption = "Sources: HDB Property Information and Existing Building (data.gov.sg); station coordinates from URA via data.gov.sg.") +
  sg_crop(stations) + theme_map()
R/01_street_codes.R: linking the two HDB files 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 01_street_codes.R - link HDB Property Information to HDB Existing Building
#
# The two data.gov.sg files describe the same blocks but share no key:
#   Property Information: blk_no, street (abbreviated name), dwelling units
#   Existing Building:    BLK_NO, ST_COD (a street code), POSTAL_COD, footprint
# ST_COD is one code per street (657 street names, 660 codes), so one geocoded
# block per street is enough to learn the street -> ST_COD crosswalk. Each
# street's block is looked up in the OneMap search API, its postal code is
# matched to a footprint, and that footprint's ST_COD becomes the street's code.
#
# About 660 API calls, spaced 1.2 s apart; results are cached in
# data/derived/street_codes.csv, so a re-run only fetches what is missing.
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/:  Rscript R/01_street_codes.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(tidyverse); library(httr2)
})

bldg <- st_read("data/raw/HDBExistingBuilding.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |> select(BLK_NO, ST_COD, POSTAL_COD)
prop <- read_csv("data/raw/HDBPropertyInformation.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cache_f <- "data/derived/street_codes.csv"
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
cache <- if (file.exists(cache_f)) read_csv(cache_f, show_col_types = FALSE,
                                            col_types = cols(.default = "c")) else
  tibble(street = character(), blk_no = character(), postal = character(),
         road_name = character(), ST_COD = character())

onemap <- function(q) {
  r <- request("https://www.onemap.gov.sg/api/common/elastic/search") |>
    req_url_query(searchVal = q, returnGeom = "Y", getAddrDetails = "Y", pageNum = 1) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 4, backoff = \(i) 5 * i,
              is_transient = \(resp) resp_status(resp) %in% c(429, 500, 502, 503)) |>
    req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE) |>
    req_perform()
  if (!grepl("json", resp_content_type(r))) return(NULL)
  resp_body_json(r)$results
}

todo <- setdiff(unique(prop$street), cache$street)
message(length(todo), " streets to look up")

for (s in todo) {
  # Try up to three of the street's blocks until one resolves to a footprint.
  blks <- head(prop$blk_no[prop$street == s], 3)
  hit <- NULL
  for (b in blks) {
    Sys.sleep(1.2)
    res <- onemap(paste(b, s))
    if (is.null(res)) next
    for (x in res) {
      if (!identical(x$BLK_NO, b) || x$POSTAL == "NIL") next
      m <- bldg[bldg$POSTAL_COD == x$POSTAL & bldg$BLK_NO == b, ]
      if (nrow(m) == 1) { hit <- tibble(street = s, blk_no = b, postal = x$POSTAL,
                                        road_name = x$ROAD_NAME, ST_COD = m$ST_COD); break }
    }
    if (!is.null(hit)) break
  }
  if (is.null(hit)) hit <- tibble(street = s, blk_no = NA, postal = NA, road_name = NA, ST_COD = NA)
  cache <- bind_rows(cache, hit)
  write_csv(cache, cache_f)
}

message(sum(!is.na(cache$ST_COD)), " of ", nrow(cache), " streets matched to a street code")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Second pass: residential blocks the crosswalk could not place on a footprint
# (two streets OneMap could not resolve, and blocks newer than the footprint
# file, mostly in Tengah). Each is geocoded on its own and kept as a point.
# Cached in data/derived/block_points.csv.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
res <- prop |> filter(residential == "Y") |>
  left_join(select(cache, street, ST_COD), by = "street") |>
  left_join(bldg, by = c("blk_no" = "BLK_NO", "ST_COD"))
miss <- res |> filter(is.na(POSTAL_COD)) |> distinct(blk_no, street)

pts_f <- "data/derived/block_points.csv"
pts <- if (file.exists(pts_f)) read_csv(pts_f, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) else
  tibble(blk_no = character(), street = character(), postal = character(), x = character(), y = character())
todo2 <- anti_join(miss, pts, by = c("blk_no", "street"))
message(nrow(todo2), " unplaced blocks to geocode")
for (k in seq_len(nrow(todo2))) {
  b <- todo2$blk_no[k]; s <- todo2$street[k]
  Sys.sleep(1.2)
  res_k <- onemap(paste(b, s))
  hit <- Filter(\(x) identical(x$BLK_NO, b), res_k %||% list())
  row <- if (length(hit)) tibble(blk_no = b, street = s, postal = hit[[1]]$POSTAL,
                                 x = hit[[1]]$X, y = hit[[1]]$Y) else
    tibble(blk_no = b, street = s, postal = NA, x = NA, y = NA)
  pts <- bind_rows(pts, row)
  write_csv(pts, pts_f)
}
message(sum(!is.na(pts$x)), " of ", nrow(pts), " unplaced blocks geocoded to a point")

4.2 Stations and the passenger data

The passenger data decides which stations exist, not any station list. Three traps had to be cleared.

  • Stations listed as planned that are already open. Keppel, Cantonment and Prince Edward Road (Circle Line stage 6, opened on 12 July 2026) are listed as future stations but carry passengers in all three months. They are moved to today’s network, together with the new Circle Line codes at Marina Bay (CC33) and Bayfront (CC34).
  • Stations that are built but not open. LTA’s own September 2026 station layer contains platforms at Bukit Brown, Mount Pleasant, Marina South and Founders’ Memorial, and a dozen depots, none of which board a passenger. Using that layer as the network would have added exactly the kind of unopened station the brief describes.
  • Joint codes. The passenger data records an interchange under one combined code (“NS27/CC33/TE20”), and in one case (Stevens) under two separate codes. Each code is mapped to its station, and all 185 codes are used once.

Station locations agree with LTA’s station outlines: for the 214 codes in both, the median distance is 0 m and the largest 86 m. Morning boardings are stable from month to month (the correlation of log tap-ins between August and October is 0.993), so averaging the three months loses little.

4.3 Which stations the model is fitted to

36 stations have fewer than 1,000 HDB dwelling units within 1 km. Some serve private estates (Newton, Stevens, Sixth Avenue, Siglap), some industry (the four Tuas stations, Joo Koon), the airport or the central area. Newton and Kranji each board over 200,000 people a month in the morning with no HDB block within a kilometre. A model whose only source of riders is HDB flats cannot explain them.

So these stations stay in every block’s choice set, where they compete for HDB riders like any other station, but their observed boardings are not used to fit the model. The data support the rule (Figure 1): the 148 fitted stations board 1.31 morning tap-ins for every tap-out; the excluded ones only 0.43.

The rule is a trade-off, and section 9 measures it. Dropping it entirely, so that the model must also explain private-estate, central and industrial stations, makes it worse at the residential stations it can explain and changes its predictions for the new stations by 15%. Setting the threshold at 500 or 2,000 instead of 1,000 changes little.

4.4 Attraction variables

Each station’s attractiveness is described by four things counted within 400 m, about a five-minute walk:

  • lines served (today’s for calibration, the planned network’s for prediction);
  • bus stops, as a measure of feeder connections;
  • points of interest: shops, food outlets, offices, schools, clinics and civic amenities in OpenStreetMap (mapped areas such as malls are reduced to one point each);
  • LRT-only: whether the station is served only by a light rail line.

Counts enter as log(1 + count). The four variables are not strongly related to each other: the largest correlation is 0.34 and every variance inflation factor is below 1.4, so their effects can be estimated separately.

4.5 The two spatial interaction data frames

The model works on a table with one row for each block and each station it could reasonably use. A block’s choice set is every station within 3 km, plus its three nearest stations if fewer are that close, so that blocks far from the network (Tengah has no station today) still have a choice. The median block has ten candidate stations. Distances under 100 m are set to 100 m, so that a block next to a station does not get an infinitely strong pull.

code 
si_now <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds")); si_30 <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "si_2030.rds"))
tibble(table = c("si_existing", "si_2030"), rows = c(nrow(si_now), nrow(si_30)),
       origins = c(n_distinct(si_now$origin_id), n_distinct(si_30$origin_id)),
       destinations = c(n_distinct(si_now$name), n_distinct(si_30$name)),
       `median choices per block` = c(median(table(si_now$origin_id)), median(table(si_30$origin_id)))) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
head(si_30 |> mutate(dist = round(dist)), 4) |> kable()
R/02_osm_poi.R, R/prep_functions.R and R/03_prepare.R: stations, attractions and the data frames 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 02_osm_poi.R - points of interest for Singapore from the Geofabrik extract
#
# The extract covers Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei (about 250 MB). GDAL's OSM
# driver reads it directly; a bounding-box filter keeps Singapore and a strip
# of Johor, which is clipped away against the Master Plan 2019 subzones.
#
# Each POI is the point itself or the centroid of a mapped area (many shops,
# schools and malls are drawn as building outlines, not points), classified
# into a few broad groups from its OSM tags.
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/:  Rscript R/02_osm_poi.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse) })
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

pbf <- "data/raw/malaysia-singapore-brunei-latest.osm.pbf"
out <- "data/derived/osm_poi_sg.gpkg"
if (!file.exists(out)) {
  bb <- c("-spat", "103.59", "1.15", "104.10", "1.48")
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
  sf::gdal_utils("vectortranslate", pbf, tmp,
                 options = c(bb, "-nln", "points", "points"),
                 config_options = c(OSM_MAX_TMPFILE_SIZE = "1024"))
  sf::gdal_utils("vectortranslate", pbf, tmp,
                 options = c(bb, "-update", "-nln", "areas",
                             "-where", "amenity IS NOT NULL OR shop IS NOT NULL OR office IS NOT NULL OR tourism IS NOT NULL OR leisure IS NOT NULL",
                             "multipolygons"),
                 config_options = c(OSM_MAX_TMPFILE_SIZE = "1024"))

  tag <- function(other, key) str_match(other, paste0('"', key, '"=>"([^"]*)"'))[, 2]
  pts <- st_read(tmp, "points", quiet = TRUE) |>
    mutate(amenity = tag(other_tags, "amenity"), shop = tag(other_tags, "shop"),
           office = tag(other_tags, "office"), tourism = tag(other_tags, "tourism"),
           leisure = tag(other_tags, "leisure"), healthcare = tag(other_tags, "healthcare"),
           source = "point") |>
    filter(!is.na(amenity) | !is.na(shop) | !is.na(office) | !is.na(tourism) |
             !is.na(leisure) | !is.na(healthcare))
  areas <- st_read(tmp, "areas", quiet = TRUE) |>
    mutate(healthcare = tag(other_tags, "healthcare"), source = "area") |>
    st_make_valid() |> st_transform(3414) |> st_point_on_surface() |> st_transform(4326)
  keep <- c("osm_id", "name", "amenity", "shop", "office", "tourism", "leisure", "healthcare", "source")
  areas$osm_id <- coalesce(areas$osm_id, areas$osm_way_id)
  poi <- bind_rows(select(pts, any_of(keep)), select(areas, any_of(keep))) |>
    st_transform(3414)

  sg <- st_read("data/raw/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSea.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
    st_transform(3414) |> st_union() |> st_make_valid()
  poi <- poi[lengths(st_intersects(poi, sg)) > 0, ]

  food <- c("restaurant", "fast_food", "cafe", "food_court", "bar", "pub", "ice_cream", "bbq")
  edu <- c("school", "college", "university", "kindergarten", "childcare", "library", "prep_school")
  health <- c("clinic", "hospital", "doctors", "dentist", "pharmacy")
  civic <- c("place_of_worship", "community_centre", "police", "post_office", "townhall", "bank", "marketplace")
  poi <- poi |> mutate(group = case_when(
    !is.na(shop) ~ "retail",
    amenity %in% food ~ "food",
    !is.na(office) ~ "office",
    amenity %in% edu ~ "education",
    amenity %in% health | !is.na(healthcare) ~ "health",
    amenity %in% civic ~ "civic",
    !is.na(leisure) | !is.na(tourism) ~ "leisure",
    TRUE ~ "other"))
  write_sf(poi, out, delete_dsn = TRUE)
}
poi <- st_read(out, quiet = TRUE)
print(count(st_drop_geometry(poi), group, sort = TRUE))

# Bus stops from OpenStreetMap: a fallback only, used if LTA's
# BusStopLocation file is not in data/raw.
bus_out <- "data/derived/osm_busstops_sg.gpkg"
if (!file.exists(bus_out)) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
  sf::gdal_utils("vectortranslate", pbf, tmp,
                 options = c("-spat", "103.59", "1.15", "104.10", "1.48",
                             "-where", "highway = 'bus_stop'", "-nln", "bus", "points"))
  sg <- st_read("data/raw/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSea.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
    st_transform(3414) |> st_union() |> st_make_valid()
  bus <- st_read(tmp, "bus", quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(3414) |> select(osm_id, name)
  write_sf(bus[lengths(st_intersects(bus, sg)) > 0, ], bus_out, delete_dsn = TRUE)
}
message(nrow(st_read(bus_out, quiet = TRUE)), " OpenStreetMap bus stops")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# prep_functions.R - the station and catchment rules, shared by R/03_prepare.R
# and the phased network scenarios (R/05b_phased_scenarios.R), so that every
# scenario is built with exactly the same definitions.
# Expects in the calling environment: origins, subzone, poi_sf, busstop.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Which line a station code belongs to. Branches and extensions count as their
# parent line (CG is the East-West Line's Changi branch, CE the Circle Line's
# extension), so a station on both is not counted as an interchange.
line_of <- function(code) {
  p <- str_extract(code, "^[A-Z]+")
  case_when(p %in% c("EW", "CG") ~ "EW", p %in% c("CC", "CE") ~ "CC",
            p == "BP" ~ "BPLRT", p %in% c("SE", "SW", "STC") ~ "SKLRT",
            p %in% c("PE", "PW", "PTC") ~ "PGLRT", p %in% JRL_PREFIX ~ "JRL",
            p %in% c("CR", "CP") ~ "CRL", TRUE ~ p)
}

# One destination per physical station: codes are grouped by station name.
complex_of <- function(df) df |>
  group_by(name = station_name) |>
  summarise(codes = paste(sort(station_code), collapse = "/"),
            lines = paste(sort(unique(line)), collapse = "+"),
            n_lines = n_distinct(line),
            lrt_only = all(str_detect(line, "LRT")),
            lon = mean(lon), lat = mean(lat), .groups = "drop") |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS)

count_within <- function(stn, x, d) lengths(st_is_within_distance(stn, x, d))
du_within <- function(stn, d) sapply(st_is_within_distance(stn, origins, d), \(i) sum(origins$du[i]))
add_attrac <- function(stn) {
  stn |> mutate(
    du_1km = du_within(stn, 1000),
    bus_stops = count_within(stn, busstop, CATCH_M),
    poi = count_within(stn, poi_sf, CATCH_M),
    poi_office = count_within(stn, filter(poi_sf, group == "office"), CATCH_M),
    poi_retail_food = count_within(stn, filter(poi_sf, group %in% c("retail", "food")), CATCH_M)) |>
    st_join(subzone, join = st_nearest_feature)
}

# One row per origin and candidate station: the stations within
# CHOICE_RADIUS_M, topped up to the K_MIN nearest.
si_frame <- function(orig, stn, radius = CHOICE_RADIUS_M) {
  D <- st_distance(orig, stn) |> units::drop_units()
  keep <- D <= radius
  r <- t(apply(D, 1, rank, ties.method = "first")) <= K_MIN
  idx <- which(keep | r, arr.ind = TRUE)
  tibble(origin_id = orig$origin_id[idx[, 1]], name = stn$name[idx[, 2]],
         dist = pmax(D[idx], MIN_DIST_M)) |>
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(select(orig, origin_id, du)), by = "origin_id")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 03_prepare.R - origins, destinations and the spatial interaction data frames
#
# Builds, in data/derived/:
#   origins.rds        HDB residential blocks with dwelling units (local market potential)
#   stations.rds       station complexes, existing and planned, with attraction variables
#   ridership.rds      observed weekday AM-peak and all-day tap-ins per existing station
#   si_existing.rds    origin x destination pairs for today's network
#   si_2030.rds        the same with the JRL and CRL phase 1 stations added
#
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/ after 00 to 02:  Rscript R/03_prepare.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse) })
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/prep_functions.R")
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

subzone <- st_read(F_SUBZONE, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |> st_make_valid() |>
  select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N)

# 1. Origins -----------------------------------------------------------------------
bldg <- st_read(F_BLDG, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |> st_make_valid()
prop <- read_csv(F_PROP, show_col_types = FALSE)
codes <- read_csv(file.path(DER, "street_codes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
pts <- read_csv(file.path(DER, "block_points.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

res <- prop |> filter(residential == "Y", total_dwelling_units >= MIN_DU) |>
  left_join(select(codes, street, ST_COD), by = "street")
on_fp <- res |> inner_join(select(bldg, BLK_NO, ST_COD, POSTAL_COD, geometry),
                           by = c("blk_no" = "BLK_NO", "ST_COD")) |>
  st_as_sf() |> st_point_on_surface() |> mutate(placed = "footprint")
as_pt <- res |> anti_join(st_drop_geometry(on_fp), by = c("blk_no", "street")) |>
  inner_join(pts, by = c("blk_no", "street")) |>
  mutate(POSTAL_COD = postal, x = as.numeric(x), y = as.numeric(y)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = STUDY_CRS) |> mutate(placed = "geocoded point")

origins <- bind_rows(on_fp, as_pt) |>
  transmute(origin_id = paste(blk_no, street, sep = " | "), blk_no, street,
            town = bldg_contract_town, year_completed, du = total_dwelling_units, placed) |>
  st_join(subzone, join = st_nearest_feature)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(origins$origin_id))
write_rds(origins, file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
message(nrow(origins), " origins, ", sum(origins$du), " dwelling units")

# 2. Observed ridership ---------------------------------------------------------------
# LTA's Passenger Volume by Train Stations: tap-ins and tap-outs per station
# code, day type and hour, one file per month. A station's tap-ins are its
# boardings, which is what the model predicts.
pv_files <- Sys.glob(file.path(RAW, PV_GLOB))
if (length(pv_files) == 0) stop("No station passenger volume file in data/raw: run R/00_download.R with DATAMALL_KEY set")
pv <- map_dfr(pv_files, \(z) read_csv(z, show_col_types = FALSE,
              col_types = cols(.default = "c", TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME = "d", TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME = "d")))
# All months DataMall serves are kept and averaged: one month can carry a
# disruption or a school holiday, and the month-to-month agreement is itself a
# data-quality check (reported in the technical report).
od_month <- paste(range(pv$YEAR_MONTH), collapse = " to ")
day_keep <- DAY_TYPE
taps_month <- pv |>
  mutate(hour = as.integer(TIME_PER_HOUR), wk = DAY_TYPE == day_keep) |>
  group_by(YEAR_MONTH, pt_code = PT_CODE) |>
  summarise(tap_am = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[wk & hour %in% AM_HOURS]),
            tapout_am = sum(TOTAL_TAP_OUT_VOLUME[wk & hour %in% AM_HOURS]),
            tap_wkday = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME[wk]),
            tap_all = sum(TOTAL_TAP_IN_VOLUME), .groups = "drop")
write_rds(taps_month, file.path(DER, "taps_by_month.rds"))
taps <- taps_month |> group_by(pt_code) |>
  summarise(across(c(starts_with("tap_"), tapout_am), \(x) sum(x) / n_distinct(pv$YEAR_MONTH)),
            .groups = "drop")

# 3. Station complexes -------------------------------------------------------------
# One destination per physical station: an interchange is one place to a rider
# walking from home, whatever the number of lines. Codes are grouped by name.
op  <- read_csv(F_STN_OP, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(status = "operational")
fut <- read_csv(F_STN_FUT, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(status = "planned")
od_codes <- unique(unlist(strsplit(taps$pt_code, "/")))
# Planned stations that the passenger data shows are already running are moved
# to the existing network (e.g. if Circle Line stage 6 has opened).
now_open <- intersect(setdiff(od_codes, op$station_code), fut$station_code)
# Codes in the passenger data that neither list has (Circle Line stage 6
# platforms at Marina Bay and Bayfront) are attached to the station their
# joint code already names, so the interchange counts the extra line.
known <- c(op$station_code, fut$station_code)
extra <- map_dfr(setdiff(od_codes, known), \(cd) {
  grp <- strsplit(taps$pt_code[str_detect(taps$pt_code, paste0("(^|/)", cd, "($|/)"))][1], "/")[[1]]
  host <- op |> filter(station_code %in% grp) |> slice(1)
  if (nrow(host)) host |> mutate(station_code = cd) else NULL
})
codes_all <- bind_rows(op, extra, filter(fut, station_code %in% now_open) |> mutate(status = "operational"),
                       filter(fut, !station_code %in% now_open) |> mutate(status = "planned")) |>
  mutate(line = line_of(station_code),
         scenario = case_when(status == "operational" ~ "existing",
                              station_code %in% JRL_LATER ~ "later",
                              str_extract(station_code, "^[A-Z]+") %in% JRL_PREFIX ~ "JRL",
                              station_code %in% CRL1_CODES ~ "CRL1", TRUE ~ "later"))


stn_now  <- complex_of(filter(codes_all, scenario == "existing")) |> mutate(new = FALSE)
stn_2030 <- complex_of(filter(codes_all, scenario %in% c("existing", "JRL", "CRL1"))) |>
  mutate(new = !name %in% stn_now$name)
unmatched <- setdiff(od_codes, codes_all$station_code[codes_all$scenario == "existing"])
if (length(unmatched)) warning("Codes in passenger data with no station: ", paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "))

# Observed tap-ins per complex: the passenger data codes interchanges jointly
# ("NS1/EW24"), so each data code is mapped to the complex of the first of
# its parts that the station list knows.
code2name <- setNames(codes_all$station_name, codes_all$station_code)
first_known <- function(code) {
  nm <- code2name[strsplit(code, "/")[[1]]]
  nm[!is.na(nm)][1] %||% NA_character_
}
ridership <- taps |> mutate(name = map_chr(pt_code, first_known)) |>
  filter(!is.na(name)) |> group_by(name) |>
  summarise(across(c(starts_with("tap_"), tapout_am), sum), pv_codes = paste(pt_code, collapse = " + "),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(month = od_month)
write_rds(ridership, file.path(DER, "ridership.rds"))
write_rds(codes_all, file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds"))

# 4. Attraction variables -----------------------------------------------------------
poi_sf <- st_read(F_POI, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |> filter(group %in% POI_GROUPS)
busstop <- if (file.exists(F_BUSSTOP)) {
  shp <- grep("\\.shp$", unzip(F_BUSSTOP, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)[1]
  st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", F_BUSSTOP, "/", shp), quiet = TRUE) |> st_set_crs(STUDY_CRS)
} else {
  warning("LTA bus stop file missing: using OpenStreetMap bus stops")
  st_read(file.path(DER, "osm_busstops_sg.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS)
}
# Line counts differ between today and 2030 at interchanges the new lines
# reach (Jurong East, Choa Chu Kang, Boon Lay, Pasir Ris, Hougang, Ang Mo Kio,
# Bright Hill): the model is calibrated on today's values and predicts with 2030's.
now_lines <- st_drop_geometry(stn_now) |>
  select(name, codes_now = codes, lines_now = lines, n_lines_now = n_lines, lrt_only_now = lrt_only)
stations <- add_attrac(stn_2030) |>
  rename(codes_2030 = codes, lines_2030 = lines, n_lines_2030 = n_lines, lrt_only_2030 = lrt_only) |>
  left_join(now_lines, by = "name") |>
  mutate(existing = name %in% stn_now$name,
         n_lines = n_lines_now, lrt_only = lrt_only_now) |>
  left_join(ridership, by = "name")
write_rds(stations, file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))

# 5. Spatial interaction data frames -------------------------------------------------
# One row per origin and candidate station: the stations within CHOICE_RADIUS_M,
# topped up to the K_MIN nearest.
write_rds(si_frame(origins, filter(stations, existing)), file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds"))
write_rds(si_frame(origins, stations), file.path(DER, "si_2030.rds"))
message("done: ", sum(stations$existing), " existing and ", sum(stations$new), " new station complexes")

5 The model

5.1 How the Huff model shares out each block’s residents

The probability that a resident of block \(i\) boards at station \(j\) is

\[ P_{ij} = \frac{A_j \, d_{ij}^{\lambda}}{\sum_{l \in C_i} A_l \, d_{il}^{\lambda}}, \qquad A_j = \exp\Big(\sum_m \gamma_m x_{jm}\Big) \]

In words: each candidate station gets a score that rises with its attractiveness \(A_j\) and falls with distance \(d_{ij}\) (in metres; \(\lambda\) is negative), and the block’s residents are shared in proportion to the scores. \(C_i\) is the block’s choice set. Attractiveness multiplies together the effects of the station’s characteristics \(x_{jm}\), which is the form of attractiveness used in an MCI model; with one distance term, the model as a whole is a Huff model.

The predicted boardings at a station are the homes it draws, times one trip rate \(k\):

\[ \hat T_j = k \sum_i DU_i \, P_{ij} \]

The fitted \(k\) is 13.2 morning boardings per dwelling unit per month, about 0.62 per weekday. It is a single number for every block, so it assumes that every HDB home produces the same number of morning trips.

Figure 3 shows what the model does for one block in Tengah.

code 
eg <- "220A | TENGAH GDN WALK"
d <- bind_rows(scn$sh_now |> filter(origin_id == eg) |> mutate(network = "Today"),
               scn$sh_30 |> filter(origin_id == eg) |> mutate(network = "With JRL and CRL phase 1")) |>
  group_by(network) |> slice_max(p, n = 5) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(new = name %in% newS$name)
ggplot(d, aes(p, reorder(name, p), fill = new)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(p)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3, colour = PAL$ink) +
  facet_wrap(~network, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = PAL$accent_lt, `TRUE` = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]]),
                    labels = c(`FALSE` = "Existing station", `TRUE` = "New JRL station"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(x = "Share of the block's residents", y = NULL) + theme_ex03(grid = "x")

5.2 Calibration

The unknowns, \(\lambda\) and the \(\gamma_m\), are chosen so that predicted boardings match observed boardings as closely as possible on the log scale, across the fitted stations. Boardings range from under a thousand to over 400,000 a month; on the log scale a 20% miss counts the same at a small station as at a large one. For any choice of the unknowns, the best \(k\) can be worked out directly, so the optimiser does not have to search for it.

Because the score inside the model is a sum of terms each multiplied by one unknown, the model is mathematically a conditional logit, and the error has an exact gradient (R/huff_core.R). That made each fit take about two seconds, which is what makes the cross-validation and bootstrap below practical. Every fit converged.

The shares were checked against MCI::huff.shares(), the course’s reference implementation: for one block they agree to the 15th decimal place (largest difference 1.7e-16). I wrote my own version only because MCI requires every block to have the same set of candidate stations, which a 3 km choice set does not give.

R/huff_core.R: the model, its error and its gradient 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# huff_core.R - the Huff model, written for fitting
#
# The probability that a resident of block i boards at station j is
#     p_ij = A_j * d_ij^lambda / sum_l (A_l * d_il^lambda)      (Huff 1963)
# summed over the stations l in block i's choice set. Attractiveness is
# multiplicative in the station's characteristics, as in an MCI model:
#     A_j = exp(sum_m gamma_m * x_jm),  x_jm = log(1 + count) or an indicator
# so the utility u_ij = lambda * log(d_ij) + sum_m gamma_m * x_jm is linear in
# the parameters: the Huff model is a conditional logit over stations. Every
# variant fitted here (one lambda, a lambda per region, exponential decay) is
# the same function of a pair-level design matrix Z with u = Z %*% theta.
#
# Predicted boardings are the dwelling units allocated to each station, scaled
# by one trip rate k so that predicted and observed totals agree on the log
# scale:  T_hat_j = k * sum_i du_i * p_ij.
#
# MCI::huff.shares() computes exactly these shares (checked in R/04); this
# version exists because the optimiser evaluates it thousands of times, and it
# supplies the analytic gradient of the loss.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pair-level design for the power-decay model: log distance, then the station
# attraction variables repeated for each pair.
huff_Z <- function(pairs, X) {
  Z <- cbind(lambda = pairs$logd, X[pairs$sj, , drop = FALSE])
  colnames(Z) <- c("lambda", colnames(X))
  Z
}

shares_Z <- function(theta, Z, oi) {
  e <- exp(drop(Z %*% theta))
  e / rowsum(e, oi, reorder = TRUE)[oi]
}

alloc_Z <- function(theta, Z, pairs, n_stn) {
  a <- rowsum(pairs$du * shares_Z(theta, Z, pairs$oi), pairs$sj, reorder = TRUE)
  out <- numeric(n_stn); out[as.integer(rownames(a))] <- a[, 1]
  out
}

# Loss: mean squared error of log boardings over the stations in fit_idx, with
# k solved in closed form. Station ridership spans three orders of magnitude,
# so a 20% miss costs the same at a small station as at a large one. Returns
# the gradient as an attribute.
loss_Z <- function(theta, Z, pairs, obs, fit_idx, grad = TRUE) {
  p <- shares_Z(theta, Z, pairs$oi)
  a <- rowsum(pairs$du * p, pairs$sj, reorder = TRUE)
  Tj <- numeric(length(obs)); Tj[as.integer(rownames(a))] <- a[, 1]
  lT <- log(pmax(Tj, 1e-12))
  F <- fit_idx
  r <- (lT[F] - mean(lT[F])) - (log(obs[F]) - mean(log(obs[F])))
  out <- mean(r^2)
  if (grad) {
    # d p_ij / d theta = p_ij (z_ij - sum_l p_il z_il)
    zbar <- rowsum(p * Z, pairs$oi, reorder = TRUE)[pairs$oi, , drop = FALSE]
    G <- rowsum(pairs$du * p * (Z - zbar), pairs$sj, reorder = TRUE)
    dlT <- matrix(0, length(obs), ncol(Z)); dlT[as.integer(rownames(G)), ] <- G / pmax(Tj[as.integer(rownames(G))], 1e-12)
    # sum(r) = 0, so the centring terms drop out of the gradient
    attr(out, "gradient") <- 2 / length(F) * colSums(r * dlT[F, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  out
}

fit_Z <- function(Z, pairs, obs, fit_idx = seq_along(obs), start = NULL) {
  if (is.null(start)) start <- c(-2, rep(0, ncol(Z) - 1))
  # Fit-index weights allow the bootstrap to repeat stations.
  opt <- optim(start, \(th) as.numeric(loss_Z(th, Z, pairs, obs, fit_idx, grad = FALSE)),
               \(th) attr(loss_Z(th, Z, pairs, obs, fit_idx), "gradient"),
               method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 1000, reltol = 1e-12))
  a <- alloc_Z(opt$par, Z, pairs, length(obs))
  k <- exp(mean(log(obs[fit_idx]) - log(pmax(a[fit_idx], 1e-12))))
  list(theta = setNames(opt$par, colnames(Z)), k = k, pred = k * a,
       loss = opt$value, convergence = opt$convergence)
}

# Wrappers for the power-decay model with station matrix X -------------------
huff_shares  <- function(theta, pairs, X) shares_Z(theta, huff_Z(pairs, X), pairs$oi)
huff_predict <- function(theta, pairs, X, n_stn) alloc_Z(theta, huff_Z(pairs, X), pairs, n_stn)
huff_fit <- function(pairs, X, obs, fit_idx = seq_along(obs), start = NULL)
  fit_Z(huff_Z(pairs, X), pairs, obs, fit_idx, start)

# Fit statistics on the log scale and the original scale.
fit_stats <- function(obs, pred) {
  tibble::tibble(
    R2_log = 1 - sum((log(obs) - log(pred))^2) / sum((log(obs) - mean(log(obs)))^2),
    RMSLE = sqrt(mean((log(pred) - log(obs))^2)),
    MdAPE_pct = 100 * median(abs(pred - obs) / obs),
    spearman = cor(obs, pred, method = "spearman"))
}

5.3 How the model is tested

Four versions of the model are compared, from simple to full:

Each is scored by 10-fold cross-validation over stations: the 148 stations are split into ten groups; each group in turn has its ridership hidden, the model is fitted on the other nine, and the hidden stations are predicted. Hidden stations stay in every choice set, so they still compete for riders; only their ridership is hidden. Everything learned from ridership, the exponents and \(k\), is learned from the nine training groups only. Nothing else depends on ridership, so no information leaks from the hidden stations into the fit.

This tests the right thing for a new station, whose location and surroundings are known and whose ridership is not. It is still not a test of a real opening, for two reasons. The hidden stations are mature, with established riding habits; a new station starts from nothing and builds up. And homes and surroundings are fixed at today’s. A true test would fit the model to data from before a station opened and compare it with ridership after. DataMall only provides the latest three months, so that cannot be done here. The three Circle Line stage 6 stations show why it matters: their morning boardings are still rising month to month, by 45% at Prince Edward Road between August and October.

6 Calibration results

6.1 Accuracy: good at ranking stations, rougher on any one station

code 
cmp |> filter(model %in% c("M0", "M1", "M2", "M3")) |>
  transmute(Model = model, `R² (log)` = round(R2_log, 2), MAE = num(MAE, 100), RMSE = num(RMSE, 100),
            `WAPE %` = round(WAPE_pct), `Bias %` = round(bias_pct), `MdAPE %` = round(MdAPE_pct),
            `Rank correlation` = round(spearman, 2)) |>
  kable()

The textbook model already explains 41% of the variation in log boardings: where the homes are does much of the work. Fitting the distance exponent alone adds nothing. Adding the number of lines raises it to 53%, and the full model to 75%.

In plain terms, the full model puts stations in nearly the right order (rank correlation 0.9), but its estimate for any one station is typically 34% off, and the absolute errors add up to 33% of all boardings. Its total for the fitted stations is 9% too high: the model is fitted on the log scale, which weighs every station equally rather than every boarding.

A high R² for existing stations does not by itself mean the model will predict new stations well. The cross-validation is the closer test, and section 5.3 explains what even that cannot test.

code 
d <- st_drop_geometry(stn)[ci, ] |> mutate(cv = cvp[ci], err = log(tap_am / cv))
lab <- d |> slice_max(abs(err), n = 10)
ggplot(d, aes(cv, tap_am)) +
  geom_abline(colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = 2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = log10(2), colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.2, linetype = 3) +
  geom_abline(intercept = -log10(2), colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.2, linetype = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = lrt_only), size = 1.9, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = name), size = 2.8, colour = PAL$ink, seed = 2, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = PAL$accent, `TRUE` = LINE_COLS[["LRT"]]),
                      labels = c(`FALSE` = "MRT", `TRUE` = "LRT only"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Predicted boardings per month (log scale)", y = "Observed tap-ins, weekdays 06:00 to 09:00, per month (log scale)") +
  theme_ex03(grid = "both")

6.2 What makes a station attractive

code 
lab_terms <- c(lambda = "Distance exponent", n_lines = "Lines served", bus_stops = "Bus stops within 400 m",
               poi = "Points of interest within 400 m", lrt_only = "LRT-only station")
p <- tibble(term = names(th), estimate = th) |> left_join(cal$ci, by = "term") |>
  mutate(term = factor(lab_terms[term], rev(lab_terms)))
ggplot(p, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = PAL$accent, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 2.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)), vjust = -0.9, size = 3, colour = PAL$ink) +
  labs(x = "Estimate (exponent on log(1 + count), or coefficient on the LRT indicator)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(grid = "x")

Turned into multipliers, and holding the other variables fixed:

  • Lines served. A station with two lines is estimated to be 2.6 times as attractive as one with one line. Saving a transfer is a plausible reason, but the model only shows the association; it cannot separate the effect of the extra line from everything else that tends to come with interchanges.
  • Points of interest. Ten times as many shops and services around a station goes with about 1.8 times the attractiveness.
  • LRT-only. An LRT-only station has about 6% of the attractiveness of an MRT station with the same characteristics. Part of this is how the data count LRT riders: a Punggol resident who boards the LRT and changes to the North East Line taps in only once.
  • Distance. Doubling the distance to a station cuts its pull by a factor of about 5.6 (exponent -2.48).
  • Bus stops. Once the other variables are in the model, the number of bus stops adds nothing that can be distinguished from zero: its interval spans zero.

One caution about reading these numbers separately. In the bootstrap, the distance exponent and the LRT effect move together (correlation 0.86): LRT stops sit very close to the blocks they serve, so the data cannot fully tell “LRT stations are less attractive” apart from “distance matters more”. Their combined effect is well determined; the split between them is not.

6.3 Where the model misses

code 
d <- stn[ci, ]
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = pmax(pmin(resid_log, 1.2), -1.2)), shape = 21, size = 2.4, colour = "white", stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = PAL$div, limits = c(-1.2, 1.2), name = "log(observed / predicted)") +
  sg_crop(stations) + theme_map()

The errors are not scattered at random: stations near each other tend to be wrong in the same direction. Moran’s I of the errors is 0.16 with each station’s six nearest neighbours (p = 0.001 in a 999-run permutation test), and it stays significant with 4, 8 or 10 neighbours (I between 0.13 and 0.22).

The largest under-predictions are city-fringe stations where HDB blocks sit among condominiums and landed homes: Novena, Great World, Katong Park, Fort Canning, Beauty World, Aljunied. The largest over-predictions are stations that opened recently (Keppel) and stations whose blocks mostly use a neighbouring station instead (Bendemeer, Labrador Park, one-north). These are explanations consistent with where the errors fall, not proven causes: the model has no data on private homes or on how long a station has been open. Section 8 tests one explanation that can be tested, that distance matters differently in different parts of Singapore.

R/04_calibrate.R and R/04b_diagnostics.R: calibration, validation and checks 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 04_calibrate.R - calibrate the Huff model on observed AM-peak boardings
#
# Four nested models, each scored in-sample and by 10-fold cross-validation
# over stations. A held-out station stays in every choice set; only its
# ridership is hidden from the fit. That is the situation of a new station,
# whose attributes are known and whose ridership is not.
#   M0  textbook default: every station equally attractive, lambda = -2 (not fitted)
#   M1  distance only: lambda fitted
#   M2  + lines served
#   M3  + bus stops, points of interest and an LRT-only indicator
# Only stations with an HDB catchment (CAL_MIN_DU_1KM) are scored; all
# stations compete in every choice set. The chosen model is checked against
# MCI::huff.shares(), bootstrapped over stations for parameter uncertainty, and
# its residuals tested for spatial autocorrelation.
#
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/ after R/03_prepare.R:  Rscript R/04_calibrate.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse); library(spdep) })
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")
set.seed(SEED)

stations <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
si <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds"))

stn <- stations |> filter(existing, !is.na(tap_am), tap_am > 0) |> arrange(name)
o_ids <- sort(unique(si$origin_id))
pairs <- si |> filter(name %in% stn$name) |>
  transmute(oi = match(origin_id, o_ids), sj = match(name, stn$name), logd = log(dist), du = du)
obs <- stn$tap_am

# Stations the residential model is judged on (see CAL_MIN_DU_1KM).
cal_idx <- which(stn$du_1km >= CAL_MIN_DU_1KM)
stn$in_fit <- seq_len(nrow(stn)) %in% cal_idx
message(length(cal_idx), " of ", nrow(stn), " stations enter the fit")

design <- function(vars, s = stn) {
  if (!length(vars)) return(matrix(numeric(0), nrow = nrow(s), ncol = 0))
  X <- sapply(vars, \(v) if (v == "lrt_only") as.numeric(s$lrt_only) else log1p(s[[v]]))
  matrix(X, nrow = nrow(s), dimnames = list(NULL, vars))
}
MODELS <- list(M1 = character(), M2 = "n_lines",
               M3 = c("n_lines", "bus_stops", "poi", "lrt_only"))
stats_on <- function(pred, idx = cal_idx) fit_stats(obs[idx], pred[idx])

# In-sample fits ---------------------------------------------------------------------
fits <- map(MODELS, \(v) huff_fit(pairs, design(v), obs, fit_idx = cal_idx))
m0_alloc <- huff_predict(-2, pairs, design(character()), length(obs))
m0_pred <- exp(mean(log(obs[cal_idx]) - log(m0_alloc[cal_idx]))) * m0_alloc
insample <- bind_rows(stats_on(m0_pred) |> mutate(model = "M0"),
                      imap_dfr(fits, \(f, nm) stats_on(f$pred) |> mutate(model = nm)))

# Cross-validation ---------------------------------------------------------------------
folds <- rep(NA_integer_, nrow(stn))
folds[cal_idx] <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = length(cal_idx)))
cv_pred <- map(MODELS, \(v) {
  X <- design(v); pred <- rep(NA_real_, length(obs))
  for (f in 1:10) {
    tr <- which(folds != f); te <- which(folds == f)
    pred[te] <- huff_fit(pairs, X, obs, fit_idx = tr)$pred[te]
  }
  pred
})
cv_m0 <- rep(NA_real_, length(obs))
for (f in 1:10) {
  tr <- which(folds != f); te <- which(folds == f)
  cv_m0[te] <- exp(mean(log(obs[tr]) - log(m0_alloc[tr]))) * m0_alloc[te]
}
cv <- bind_rows(stats_on(cv_m0) |> mutate(model = "M0"),
                imap_dfr(cv_pred, \(p, nm) stats_on(p) |> mutate(model = nm)))

params <- imap_dfr(fits, \(f, nm) tibble(model = nm, term = names(f$theta), estimate = f$theta)) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(model = "M0", term = "lambda", estimate = -2))

# Bootstrap the chosen model --------------------------------------------------------------
best <- "M3"
Xb <- design(MODELS[[best]])
boot <- map_dfr(1:200, \(b) {
  idx <- sample(cal_idx, replace = TRUE)
  f <- huff_fit(pairs, Xb, obs, fit_idx = idx, start = fits[[best]]$theta)
  tibble(b = b, term = names(f$theta), estimate = f$theta)
})
ci <- boot |> group_by(term) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(estimate, 0.025), hi = quantile(estimate, 0.975), .groups = "drop")

# Check against the MCI package -------------------------------------------------------------
th <- fits[[best]]$theta
stn$A <- exp(as.vector(Xb %*% th[-1]))
one_origin <- si |> filter(origin_id == o_ids[1], name %in% stn$name) |>
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(select(stn, name, A)), by = "name") |> as.data.frame()
assign("one_origin", one_origin, envir = globalenv())  # MCI looks its data up by name
mci <- MCI::huff.shares(one_origin, "origin_id", "name", "A", "dist", gamma = 1,
                        lambda = th[["lambda"]], dtype = "pow")
mine <- tibble(name = stn$name[pairs$sj[pairs$oi == 1]],
               p = huff_shares(th, pairs, Xb)[pairs$oi == 1])
mci_check <- max(abs(mine$p - mci$p_ij[match(mine$name, mci$name)]))

# Residuals: are the misses spatially clustered? ----------------------------------------------
stn <- stn |> mutate(pred = fits[[best]]$pred, cv_pred = cv_pred[[best]],
                     resid_log = log(obs) - log(pred))
fit_stn <- stn[cal_idx, ]
nb <- knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(fit_stn), k = 6))
moran_resid <- moran.test(fit_stn$resid_log, nb2listw(nb, style = "W"))

write_rds(list(stn = stn, fits = fits, params = params, ci = ci, boot = boot,
               insample = insample, cv = cv, cv_pred = cv_pred, cv_m0 = cv_m0, folds = folds,
               m0_pred = m0_pred, cal_idx = cal_idx, best = best, models = MODELS,
               mci_check = mci_check, moran_resid = moran_resid, o_ids = o_ids),
          file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
print(insample); print(cv); print(params, n = 20); print(ci)
message("MCI check, max |difference| in shares: ", signif(mci_check, 3))
message("Moran's I of log residuals: ", round(moran_resid$estimate[1], 3),
        " (p = ", signif(moran_resid$p.value, 3), ")")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 04b_diagnostics.R - checks on the data and the fitted model
#
# Every check here answers a question a reviewer could ask, and every number
# the report quotes about data quality or model validity comes from here:
#   - is any station counted twice, or any passenger-data code left unused?
#   - do the station coordinates agree with LTA's own station polygons?
#   - did the HDB join put two property records on one footprint?
#   - did every optimisation converge, including the bootstrap refits?
#   - is total demand conserved between scenarios (redistribution, not growth)?
#   - are the attraction variables collinear enough to destabilise exponents?
#   - is the Moran's I of the residuals robust to a permutation test?
#   - are the newly opened Circle Line stations still ramping up?
#   - what does the trip rate k mean in everyday units?
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/ after R/04:  Rscript R/04b_diagnostics.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse); library(spdep) })
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")
set.seed(SEED)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

cal      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
stations <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
origins  <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
rid      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "ridership.rds"))
taps_m   <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "taps_by_month.rds"))
D <- list()

# 1. Passenger-data codes: one row per station complex, nothing double counted
D$pv_codes_per_station <- rid |> mutate(n_codes = str_count(pv_codes, fixed(" + ")) + 1) |>
  count(n_codes, name = "stations")
D$pv_codes_total <- n_distinct(taps_m$pt_code)
D$pv_codes_used  <- sum(str_count(rid$pv_codes, fixed(" + ")) + 1)

# 2. Station coordinates against LTA's station polygons (same code)
lta <- st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", F_LTA_STN, "/TrainStation_Sep2026/RapidTransitSystemStation.shp"),
               quiet = TRUE) |> st_set_crs(STUDY_CRS) |> st_make_valid()
codes_pts <- bind_rows(read_csv(F_STN_OP, show_col_types = FALSE),
                       read_csv(F_STN_FUT, show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS)
lta_codes <- lta |> mutate(code = str_split(STN_NAM, "[/ ,]+")) |> unnest(code)
m <- inner_join(st_drop_geometry(codes_pts) |> mutate(i = row_number()),
                st_drop_geometry(lta_codes) |> mutate(k = row_number()), by = c("station_code" = "code"))
m$dist_m <- as.numeric(st_distance(codes_pts[m$i, ], lta_codes[m$k, ], by_element = TRUE))
D$coord_check <- m |> group_by(station_code, station_name) |> summarise(dist_m = min(dist_m), .groups = "drop")
D$coord_summary <- D$coord_check |> summarise(n = n(), median_m = median(dist_m),
                                              p95_m = quantile(dist_m, 0.95), max_m = max(dist_m),
                                              within_100m = mean(dist_m <= 100))

# 3. HDB join: one footprint per property record
D$origins_dup_postal <- origins |> st_drop_geometry() |> filter(placed == "footprint") |>
  count(blk_no, street) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()
D$origins_du_total <- sum(origins$du)
D$origins_empty_geom <- sum(st_is_empty(origins))
xy <- st_coordinates(origins)
D$origins_same_xy <- sum(duplicated(round(xy, 1)))

# 4. Convergence of every fit
D$convergence <- tibble(model = names(cal$fits), code = map_int(cal$fits, "convergence"))

# 5. Demand conservation and the meaning of k
scn <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "scenario.rds"))
D$conservation <- scn$res |> summarise(now = sum(pred_now, na.rm = TRUE), y2030 = sum(pred_2030)) |>
  mutate(diff_pct = 100 * (y2030 / now - 1))
k <- cal$fits[[cal$best]]$k
D$k <- k
# k is monthly AM-peak boardings per dwelling unit; per weekday it divides by
# the average number of weekdays in the three months.
# Monday-to-Friday days: 21, 22 and 22. National Day (9 Aug 2026) falls on a
# Sunday, so Monday 10 Aug is the holiday, which DataMall counts with weekends.
wk <- c(`2026-08` = 20, `2026-09` = 22, `2026-10` = 22)
D$k_per_weekday <- k / mean(wk)

# 6. Collinearity of the attraction variables (fitted stations)
stn <- cal$stn[cal$cal_idx, ] |> st_drop_geometry()
X <- tibble(n_lines = log1p(stn$n_lines), bus_stops = log1p(stn$bus_stops),
            poi = log1p(stn$poi), lrt_only = as.numeric(stn$lrt_only))
D$cor_X <- cor(X)
D$vif <- map_dbl(names(X), \(v) 1 / (1 - summary(lm(reformulate(setdiff(names(X), v), v), data = X))$r.squared)) |>
  set_names(names(X))
D$boot_cor <- cal$boot |> pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) |> select(-b) |> cor()

# 7. Moran's I: analytical (randomisation) and permutation
fit_stn <- cal$stn[cal$cal_idx, ]
lw <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(fit_stn), k = 6)), style = "W")
D$moran_perm <- moran.mc(fit_stn$resid_log, lw, nsim = 999)
D$moran_k <- map_dfr(c(4, 6, 8, 10), \(kk) {
  lwk <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(fit_stn), k = kk)), style = "W")
  mt <- moran.mc(fit_stn$resid_log, lwk, nsim = 999)
  tibble(k = kk, I = mt$statistic, p = mt$p.value)
})

# 8. Circle Line stage 6: ramp-up across the three months
D$ccl6 <- taps_m |> filter(str_detect(pt_code, "CC30|CC31|CC32")) |>
  select(YEAR_MONTH, pt_code, tap_am, tap_wkday)

# 9. Residuals against station characteristics (association only)
D$resid_by_group <- fit_stn |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(group = case_when(lrt_only ~ "LRT only", n_lines > 1 ~ "Interchange",
                           REGION_N == "CENTRAL REGION" ~ "Central, one line", TRUE ~ "Other, one line")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_resid = median(resid_log), mean_resid = mean(resid_log), .groups = "drop")

write_rds(D, file.path(DER, "diagnostics.rds"))
str(D[c("pv_codes_per_station", "pv_codes_total", "pv_codes_used", "coord_summary", "origins_dup_postal",
        "origins_du_total", "origins_same_xy", "convergence", "conservation", "k", "k_per_weekday", "vif")], max.level = 2)
print(round(D$cor_X, 2)); print(round(D$boot_cor, 2)); print(D$moran_perm); print(D$moran_k)
print(D$ccl6); print(D$resid_by_group); print(D$coord_check |> arrange(-dist_m) |> head(8))

7 Predictions for the expanded network

7.1 Which network

The brief asks for today’s network compared with today’s network plus the JRL and the CRL phase 1, and describes that as the network by 2030. That comparison is the main one in this report and the slides. Whether it is literally the 2030 network depends on LTA’s current schedules, which are recorded with their sources in future_station_schedule.csv and used to build two further networks (R/05b_phased_scenarios.R):

code 
lab_scn <- c(brief = "Brief: today + JRL + CRL phase 1", end_2030 = "End of 2030, by LTA's current schedules",
             full = "Every planned station in the station list")
ph$summary |> mutate(Network = lab_scn[scenario]) |>
  transmute(Network, Stations = stations, `New stations` = new_stations,
            `Boardings at new stations, per month` = num(new_boardings, 1000)) |>
  kable()

LTA’s published schedules, checked on 14 November 2026, put the JRL’s three stages in 2028 and 2029 (LTA says the dates for stages 2 and 3 will be updated) and the CRL phase 1 by 2030. So the brief’s network matches the official plan for the end of 2030, with two corrections.

  • JS2A is not part of it. The station list includes JS2A (between Choa Chu Kang West and Tengah), an infill station LTA announced in March 2026 and plans to open in the mid-2030s, when the area around it is developed. It is not one of the JRL’s 24 stations, and the brief’s network here leaves it out. (The station list calls it “Forest Hill”; LTA has not published a name.)
  • Other lines also open before 2030. Bedok South, Sungei Bedok and Xilin open on 26 December 2026, and Founders’ Memorial is to open with the memorial, which is due at the end of 2028 (the year is inferred from the memorial’s schedule, not stated by LTA). They are in the end-2030 network but not in the brief’s.

Adding those four stations hardly affects the JRL and CRL results: the new stations’ ranking is unchanged (rank correlation 1.00) and their total changes by less than 0.1%. The extra stations are in the east, far from both lines; the existing station most affected by them is Bayshore (-33%). So the brief’s comparison is a fair stand-in for the end-2030 network for this question. The full planned network, which also adds the CRL phase 2 and Punggol extension (2032), Brickland (2034), Sungei Kadut (2035), the Changi Terminal 5 stations (mid-2030s) and stations with no announced date, is shown in Table 7 only for completeness: it is not a forecast of any particular year.

7.2 Morning boardings at the new stations

code 
q <- quantile(stn$tap_am[ci], c(0.1, 0.5))
d <- res |> filter(new) |> mutate(name = reorder(name, pred_2030),
                                 line = ifelse(line_new == "JRL", "Jurong Region Line", "Cross Island Line"))
ggplot(d, aes(pred_2030, name)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = q[1], xmax = q[2], ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = PAL$land, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pred_2030_lo, xmax = pred_2030_hi, colour = line), height = 0, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = line), size = 2.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Modelled boardings per month from HDB homes, weekdays 06:00 to 09:00 (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(grid = "x")

The new stations with the most modelled morning boardings are those placed among HDB blocks that have no station of their own today. Tengah Plantation (180,000 a month) is the clearest case: Tengah’s 16,318 dwelling units are 1.3 to 2.2 km (median 1.7 km) in a straight line from the nearest station today. On the CRL, Serangoon North (172,000) and Pasir Ris East (116,000) serve large estates between today’s lines.

7 new stations fall below the 10th percentile of today’s fitted stations: Tukang, Nanyang Gateway, Peng Kang Hill, Loyang, Jurong Hill, Jurong Pier, Aviation Park. Most are in the Jurong Innovation District, at the university or near the airport. This shows that few HDB residents live near them; it does not show that they will be little used. They are built for jobs, campuses and the airport, and that demand would appear as people arriving in the morning (tap-outs), which this model does not estimate. Their surroundings will also change by the time they open, in either direction, so today’s figure is neither a floor nor a ceiling.

7.3 How the new lines redistribute boardings at existing stations

The model holds the number of homes and the trip rate fixed, so adding stations cannot add boardings: the total predicted morning boardings are the same in both networks (the difference is 0%). What changes is where people board. So every change below is a reallocation of modelled HDB-origin morning boardings.

code 
d <- res |> filter(existing, !is.na(change)) |>
  filter(rank(change) <= 15 | change > 0) |>
  mutate(name = reorder(name, change), dir = ifelse(change > 0, "gain", "loss"))
ggplot(d, aes(change, name, fill = dir)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(change_pct), hjust = ifelse(change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)), size = 2.9, colour = PAL$ink) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(gain = PAL$accent, loss = PAL$loss), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.18, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = "Change in modelled boardings per month, weekdays 06:00 to 09:00", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(grid = "x")
code 
d <- stations |> select(name) |> left_join(res, by = "name")
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(d, existing, !is.na(change_pct)),
          aes(fill = pmin(pmax(change_pct, -0.6), 0.3), size = pred_now), shape = 21, colour = "white", stroke = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(d, new), aes(colour = line_new), shape = 18, size = 2.4) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c(PAL$loss, "#D88C74", PAL$loss_lt, "#B9BEC6", PAL$accent), values = rescale(c(-0.6, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.3)),
                       limits = c(-0.6, 0.3), labels = label_percent(), name = "Change") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(JRL = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], CRL = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = "New station") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, guide = "none") +
  sg_crop(stations) + theme_map()

The losses fall where the new lines run between existing stations rather than beyond them. In the west, the JRL’s Jurong West branch takes blocks that today use Chinese Garden, Lakeside, Pioneer and Boon Lay, and the Tengah stations take blocks from Bukit Batok and Bukit Gombak. In the north-east, Serangoon North and Tavistock take blocks from Kovan and Serangoon. The only stations that gain are the four that become Cross Island Line interchanges: Hougang, Bright Hill, Ang Mo Kio and Pasir Ris.

What these numbers do not say is as important. Fewer people entering Lakeside does not mean emptier trains past Lakeside: many residents who now board the JRL will still change to the East-West Line at Jurong East or Boon Lay. Train loads depend on the routes people take and on train capacity, which this model does not represent. The changes describe station access (where people enter the network), not crowding.

7.4 How catchments change

code 
west <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = 11000, xmax = 23500, ymin = 31000, ymax = 42500), crs = st_crs(STUDY_CRS)))
o_w <- origins |> st_filter(west) |> left_join(scn$dom, by = "origin_id")
top <- union(names(sort(table(o_w$station_now), decreasing = TRUE))[1:12], names(sort(table(o_w$station_2030), decreasing = TRUE))[1:14])
pal_st <- setNames(rep_len(c("#137C8B", "#B4432F", "#5E7CA4", "#C9913D", "#4E8F5A", "#8A5A8C", "#2F6F86", "#C76B4F",
                             "#7A8F3C", "#9C6B3F", "#3E7F72", "#A2546C", "#5C6C99", "#B08A2E", "#6F5A9A", "#3F8A5C"), length(top)), top)
stn_w <- st_filter(lines_sf(stations), west)
o_w <- o_w |> mutate(change = case_when(to_new ~ "Switches to a new station",
                                       switched ~ "Switches to another existing station",
                                       TRUE ~ "Keeps its station"))
p_now <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = ifelse(station_now %in% top, station_now, "other")), size = 0.7) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = "white") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pal_st, other = PAL$null), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Today") + theme_map() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
p_30 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = change), size = 0.7) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, !existing), aes(fill = kind), shape = 23, size = 2.4, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Switches to a new station" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]],
                                 "Switches to another existing station" = PAL$loss,
                                 "Keeps its station" = PAL$null), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), guide = "none") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  labs(title = "With the JRL and CRL phase 1") + theme_map() + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
(p_now + p_30) & theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA))

Across Singapore, 1,342 of the 10,817 blocks change their main station, 1,042 of them to a new one. The west changes most: Tengah’s blocks, which today sit at the edge of several catchments, get stations of their own, and the Jurong West estates divide among four JRL stations.

R/05_scenario.R and R/05b_phased_scenarios.R: the expanded networks 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 05_scenario.R - the 2030 network: JRL and CRL phase 1 added
#
# The calibrated model is applied twice to the same 10,817 HDB blocks: once to
# today's stations and once to the 2030 set, in which the new stations exist and
# the interchanges they create count their extra line. Comparing the two runs
# of the same model isolates the effect of the new stations; comparing either
# with observed ridership would mix it with the model's own error.
#
# Prediction intervals come from the bootstrap draws of R/04_calibrate.R: each
# draw's parameters are re-scaled to the observed total and re-applied.
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/ after R/04:  Rscript R/05_scenario.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse) })
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")

cal <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
stations <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "stations.rds")) |> arrange(name)
si_now <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "si_existing.rds"))
si_30  <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "si_2030.rds"))
best <- cal$best; vars <- cal$models[[best]]; th <- cal$fits[[best]]$theta; k <- cal$fits[[best]]$k

stn_now <- filter(stations, existing)
stn_30  <- stations |> mutate(n_lines = n_lines_2030, lrt_only = lrt_only_2030)

design_for <- function(stn) {
  if (!length(vars)) return(matrix(numeric(0), nrow = nrow(stn), ncol = 0))
  X <- sapply(vars, \(v) if (v == "lrt_only") as.numeric(stn$lrt_only) else log1p(stn[[v]]))
  matrix(X, nrow = nrow(stn), dimnames = list(NULL, vars))
}
pairs_for <- function(si, stn) {
  o_ids <- sort(unique(si$origin_id))
  si |> filter(name %in% stn$name) |>
    transmute(origin_id, name, oi = match(origin_id, o_ids), sj = match(name, stn$name),
              logd = log(dist), du = du)
}
P_now <- pairs_for(si_now, stn_now); X_now <- design_for(stn_now)
P_30  <- pairs_for(si_30, stn_30);   X_30  <- design_for(stn_30)

run <- function(theta, k, P, X, n) k * huff_predict(theta, P, X, n)
pred_now <- run(th, k, P_now, X_now, nrow(stn_now))
pred_30  <- run(th, k, P_30, X_30, nrow(stn_30))

res <- stn_30 |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(name, existing, new, lines_now, lines_2030, codes_2030, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N,
         bus_stops, poi, tap_am) |>
  mutate(pred_2030 = pred_30) |>
  left_join(tibble(name = stn_now$name, pred_now = pred_now), by = "name") |>
  mutate(change = pred_2030 - pred_now, change_pct = change / pred_now,
         line_new = case_when(str_detect(lines_2030, "JRL") & new ~ "JRL",
                              str_detect(lines_2030, "CRL") & new ~ "CRL", TRUE ~ NA))

# Bootstrap intervals ----------------------------------------------------------------
obs <- cal$stn$tap_am
X_cal <- design_for(cal$stn |> arrange(name))
P_cal <- pairs_for(si_now, cal$stn |> arrange(name))
draws <- cal$boot |> pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate)
boot_pred <- map(seq_len(nrow(draws)), \(b) {
  th_b <- unlist(draws[b, names(th)])
  a <- huff_predict(th_b, P_cal, X_cal, nrow(X_cal))
  ci_ <- cal$cal_idx
  k_b <- exp(mean(log(obs[ci_]) - log(pmax(a[ci_], 1e-9))))
  tibble(name = stn_30$name, b = b, pred_2030 = run(th_b, k_b, P_30, X_30, nrow(stn_30))) |>
    left_join(tibble(name = stn_now$name, pred_now = run(th_b, k_b, P_now, X_now, nrow(stn_now))), by = "name")
}) |> list_rbind()
pi <- boot_pred |> group_by(name) |>
  summarise(pred_2030_lo = quantile(pred_2030, 0.025), pred_2030_hi = quantile(pred_2030, 0.975),
            change_lo = quantile(pred_2030 - pred_now, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
            change_hi = quantile(pred_2030 - pred_now, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
res <- left_join(res, pi, by = "name")

# Market areas -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each block's dominant station (highest share), today and in 2030, and the
# share-weighted dwelling units every station draws.
share_tbl <- function(P, X) P |> mutate(p = huff_shares(th, P, X))
sh_now <- share_tbl(P_now, X_now); sh_30 <- share_tbl(P_30, X_30)
dominant <- function(sh) sh |> group_by(origin_id) |> slice_max(p, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |> select(origin_id, station = name, p_max = p)
dom <- dominant(sh_now) |> rename(station_now = station, p_now = p_max) |>
  left_join(dominant(sh_30) |> rename(station_2030 = station, p_2030 = p_max), by = "origin_id") |>
  mutate(switched = station_now != station_2030,
         to_new = station_2030 %in% res$name[res$new])

catch <- full_join(
  sh_now |> group_by(name) |> summarise(du_now = sum(du * p), .groups = "drop"),
  sh_30 |> group_by(name) |> summarise(du_2030 = sum(du * p), .groups = "drop"), by = "name")
res <- left_join(res, catch, by = "name")

write_rds(list(res = res, dom = dom, boot_pred = boot_pred, sh_now = sh_now, sh_30 = sh_30),
          file.path(DER, "scenario.rds"))
res |> filter(new) |> arrange(-pred_2030) |> select(name, line_new, pred_2030, pred_2030_lo, pred_2030_hi) |> print(n = 40)
res |> filter(existing) |> arrange(change_pct) |> select(name, pred_now, pred_2030, change_pct) |> head(15) |> print()
message(sum(dom$switched), " blocks change dominant station; ", sum(dom$to_new), " now dominated by a new station")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 05b_phased_scenarios.R - networks defined by official opening schedules
#
# R/05 runs the comparison the brief asks for: today's network against today's
# plus the JRL and the CRL phase 1. The brief calls that the network "by 2030";
# whether it really is depends on LTA's current schedules, which are recorded,
# with sources, in future_station_schedule.csv. This script builds three
# networks from that table and runs the same calibrated model on each:
#   brief       today + JRL + CRL phase 1 (the brief's comparison, as in R/05)
#   end_2030    today + every planned station LTA currently schedules to open
#               by the end of 2030
#   full        today + every planned station in the station list
# All scenarios hold today's homes and today's surroundings fixed, so they show
# where today's HDB residents would board, not ridership in a given year.
# Run from Take-home_Ex/Take-home_Ex03/ after R/04:  Rscript R/05b_phased_scenarios.R
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(sf); library(tidyverse) })
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/prep_functions.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

cal <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
origins <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
codes_all <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "station_codes.rds"))
subzone <- st_read(F_SUBZONE, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |> st_make_valid() |>
  select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N)
poi_sf <- st_read(F_POI, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |> filter(group %in% POI_GROUPS)
busstop <- if (file.exists(F_BUSSTOP)) {
  shp <- grep("\\.shp$", unzip(F_BUSSTOP, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)[1]
  st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", F_BUSSTOP, "/", shp), quiet = TRUE) |> st_set_crs(STUDY_CRS)
} else st_read(file.path(DER, "osm_busstops_sg.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS)

sched <- read_csv(F_SCHEDULE, show_col_types = FALSE, comment = "#")
planned <- codes_all |> filter(scenario != "existing") |>
  left_join(select(sched, station_code, stage, planned_opening), by = "station_code")
missing_sched <- planned |> filter(is.na(planned_opening)) |> pull(station_code)
if (length(missing_sched)) message("No verified opening year (kept out of end_2030): ", paste(missing_sched, collapse = ", "))

scenario_codes <- list(
  brief    = c(codes_all$station_code[codes_all$scenario == "existing"],
               planned$station_code[planned$scenario %in% c("JRL", "CRL1")]),
  end_2030 = c(codes_all$station_code[codes_all$scenario == "existing"],
               planned$station_code[!is.na(planned$planned_opening) & planned$planned_opening <= 2030]),
  full     = codes_all$station_code)

existing_names <- unique(codes_all$station_name[codes_all$scenario == "existing"])
vars <- cal$models[[cal$best]]; th <- cal$fits[[cal$best]]$theta; k <- cal$fits[[cal$best]]$k
design <- function(s) {
  X <- sapply(vars, \(v) if (v == "lrt_only") as.numeric(s$lrt_only) else log1p(s[[v]]))
  matrix(X, nrow = nrow(s), dimnames = list(NULL, vars))
}
run_network <- function(code_set) {
  stn <- complex_of(filter(codes_all, station_code %in% code_set)) |> add_attrac() |> arrange(name)
  si <- si_frame(origins, stn)
  o_ids <- sort(unique(si$origin_id))
  P <- si |> transmute(oi = match(origin_id, o_ids), sj = match(name, stn$name), logd = log(dist), du)
  stn |> st_drop_geometry() |>
    transmute(name, lines, n_lines, new = !name %in% existing_names,
              pred = k * huff_predict(th, P, design(stn), nrow(stn)))
}
